About the Forensic Science event

Forensic Science is a Teamwork event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · online submission.

Ten in-depth lessons for the two-person HOSA Forensic Science event, following the 2026–27 test plan (crime scene and death investigation 20%, toxicology and pharmacology 20%, and 10% each for history and careers, anthropology, entomology, blood and biological fluids, DNA analysis and forensic psychology) and the 40-minute Round Two case analysis with its written conclusion: time of death range, immediate cause, manner, contributing conditions and evidence. Built around Bertino’s Forensic Science Fundamentals and Bell’s Forensic Science, with search-pattern and evidence sorting, time-of-death, degree-day and angle-of-impact calculations, toxicology and DNA sequencing drills and case scenarios. Descriptions are kept non-graphic; actual case materials may be graphic, so follow your advisor’s guidance.

Sample Forensic Science questions

1. Which method is used to confirm the identity of a drug after a positive screening test?

  1. A color spot test
  2. GC-MS
  3. Visual inspection only
  4. A breath test
Show answer

B. GC-MS

Screening tests are presumptive and can give false positives. GC-MS separates and identifies compounds with high certainty.

2. A body shows bright cherry-red lividity. Which poisoning is suggested?

  1. Chronic arsenic
  2. Opioid narcotics
  3. Alcohol
  4. Carbon monoxide
Show answer

D. Carbon monoxide

Carbon monoxide binds tightly to hemoglobin and forms carboxyhemoglobin, which gives the blood and lividity a cherry-red color.

3. Which search pattern is best for a large outdoor area with many searchers?

  1. Spiral search by one person
  2. Zone search of a single room
  3. Line (strip) search
  4. Wheel search
Show answer

C. Line (strip) search

Searchers walk side by side in straight lines across the area. Grid searches repeat the line search at right angles for more thoroughness.
